Two player games I play with my girlfriend:

Dao is a super simple abstract two player game.

Mr. Jack is a low luck high deduction game where one player plays Jack the Ripper, and the other tries to catch him.

Dragonheart is a two player card game. It's hard to describe, but is great for a quick play.

Summoner Wars head to head tactical combat game.

Games I play with my girlfriend that aren't exclusively 2 player:

Dominion classic deck building game that scales well no matter how many people you play with.

In the same vein is Splendor which uses similar mechanics but is simpler to play.

Pathfinder ACG co-op game. Heavily random, but fun.

Suburbia tile placing game about building your own suburb.

Takenoko lighter tile placing game about building a garden for a panda.

It's not exactly "boardgames" material but Magic:The Gathering is a fantastic two player game if you're willing to put in the time to learn how to play it.

Yes the game has been known as "cardboard crack" but you don't have to go bugfuck apeshit and spend $500 on cards if you don't want to.

They even sell specialized "Duel Decks" which are a pair of decks specifically built to be very balanced and fun to play against each other.

A pair of the "intro pack" decks would come out to about $30 retail and have a fully playable deck inside that doesn't require you to do anything other than pop the plastic, shuffle, and start playing without learning all about deck building mechanics.

The only thing I'd add to that is that if you want to keep the game as balanced as possible try to use only cards from one release (or "Edition", if that makes more sense to you) at a time. Two decks built solely out of cards from the M15 (2015 core set cards) should be fairly balanced but if you have an M15 deck playing against an M12 deck there may be some balance issues giving one deck an automatic advantage over the other. Obviously a BIG part of the game is learning how to design your decks by swapping cards in and out to make them stronger and more efficient but if you want to start with pre-built decks just keep to the same Block or Set and you'll be fine.
